A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAF study, with matching authors, method, and retained experiments. All pages are readable, including v2 Appendices A and B; v1 contains no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original ranking-manipulation experiments, objective ablations, cross-model transfer results, and prompt-length analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds GPT-5.1 transfer results, human evaluation results, and additional qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objectives, gradient-based shortlisting, entropy-based weighting, token sampling, and convergence procedure. The new analyses do not modify RAF.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds a human assessment task covering prompt fluency, persuasiveness, and manipulation detectability. The underlying STSData coverage remains books, cameras, and coffee machines; adding GPT-5.1 changes the evaluated model rather than the data domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SRP and STS, and Table 3 retains SRP. The new human study also uses SRP; excluding STS from this new study does not remove it from an existing comparison. The discussed no-injection rank of 5.5 is an expectation, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an anonymous, randomized paired human evaluation with three judgment criteria, substantially extending the evaluation design beyond automated metrics. It also evaluates transferred prompts through the GPT-5.1 API. Existing benchmark preprocessing, tuning settings, token budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends transfer testing to GPT-5.1, adds qualitative RAF failure cases in Section 4.7, and adds camera and coffee-machine prompt trajectories in Appendix B. The objective and prompt-length ablations are unchanged, and the book example is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random seeds and mean ranks for the existing experiments. V2 introduces no new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the human evaluation reports point percentages only.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged, but substantial new evidence is reported. Table 3 adds GPT-5.1 ranks of 5.76 for RAF and 5.95 for SRP. Figure 3 reports RAF versus SRP selections of 83.95% versus 9.88% for fluency, 72.84% versus 14.81% for persuasiveness, and 5.56% versus 76.54% for appearing manipulative. Appendix B adds two prompt-result examples.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, ranking and readability losses, entropy weighting, and algorithmic formulation are unchanged. V2 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about RAF, fluent ranking manipulation, open-source performance, transferability, and security implications. The new evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 now explicitly rejects a claim of reliable closed-source compromise and characterizes GPT-5.1 transfer as limited. Section 4.7 adds substantive explanations of fluent-but-ineffective continuations and mode collapse, including corpus-level detectability and proposed diversity constraints. These materially expand the stated applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses the bad-word and bad-phrase inventory. V2 also identifies the GPT-5.1 snapshot and acknowledges the Delta computing system. Existing hyperparameters and code access information remain unchanged; the inventory disclosure does not establish that earlier scoring procedures changed.

R1.justification: The ranking-manipulation discussion adds Hu (2025), Du et al. (2026), and Li et al. (2026), while retaining its research positioning. Updates to the survey and Beyond Yes and No references concern matching existing works rather than additional research contributions.

P1.justification: V2 separates open-source and closed-source transfer discussion, adds human-evaluation and failure-analysis subsections, rewrites the prompt-quality discussion, and organizes examples into appendices. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the human-evaluation bar chart, expands Table 3 with a GPT-5.1 row and revised caption, and moves the existing length plot and book-example boxes. Additional example boxes appear in Appendix B. The main diagrams, other tables, and two-column layout remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical support and scope calibration through human judgments, a closed-source transfer test, explicit failure conditions, and the disclosed detection inventory. The gains are limited by missing participant and prompt-pair counts and uncertainty reporting for the human study, plus the absence of a measured no-injection control for GPT-5.1. The original method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
